title: Wrong implementation of how to identify cookies

comments.body: assigned to you @pmlopes

This one is tricky to solve. Given that the uniqueness should be the tuple (name + domain + path) and the public API exposes just a simple `Map`, we either need to break and change it to be a `MultiMap` or define a well-known format for looking up cookies. 

Say that we define that the key in the map is the string `NAME/PATH` which is trivial to split as the path begins on the first `/`, it makes the lookup and removal more expensive as we need to consider using a `TreeMap` and perform `subMap(key, key + Character.MAX_VALUE)` to create a view filtering the prefix, and then we still need to decide how to handle more than 1 entry.
Btw It would be nice to have the add/remove functionality that exists in `HttpServerResponse` in `HttpClientRequest` as well.

@fbuetler the concern here is to reduce the blast radius of the change. I do agree that a better structure would be a better fit, I am just brainstorming how we can achieve this with the last amount of breakage.

I believe that the current API works for the most general use case, the API follows the nodejs style of having a single map based on the cookie name.

However, I understand that this isn't flexible enough to comply with the official spec. Let's try to figure out a way where the breakage is the least.

If we keep the cookies internally in a `MultiMap` then we don't lose the overlap of cookie name, lookup and removal can still be complex as we need to perform the lookup internally.

If we keep the cookies in a `MultiMap` lookup by name is still trivial as all cookies with the same name are grouped into a single bucket, it only gets complex for your specific case where you need a helper that returns all cookies for a given name. e.g.: `List<Cookie> getAllCookies(String name)`.

And to avoid ambiguity in removal a `removeCookie(Cookie[, boolean])` method should be added to explicitly match, instead of removing all cookies that match the name.

Based on what would you then decide what cookie you need to return by `getCookie(String name)` in the original API? To keep the original semantics, we would need to store the most recent cookie explicitly and return this.

And also how would the Map, returned by `cookieMap()`, look like?

`getCookie()` would just return the 1st cookie matching the given name, so the behavior would be the same as before and the `cookieMap()` just hides the multimap by returning again only the 1st entry, so the behavior is again the same as before.

Finally, the remove by `String` wipes the full matching list which again matches the old behavior and respects the contract of returning the list of matched cookies.
I may have made a mistake by mixing request and response methods in my argument above.
Agreed in both points (code snippet about multimap and first vs last).
@vietj I think we have a good compromise here. We deprecate 2 methods, and introduce 6 new ones to handle all the extra cases as per RFC spec. WDYT?

this looks good to me, I'm not sure we need to deprecate methods though as they still seem valid to me

this looks fine to me, however I think we don't need to deprecate `removeCookie(String name)` and instead just say that this will remove the first `Cookie` occurence and explain that this might not be correct in some situations and advocate to use the more precision implementation.

we could also overload `List<Cookies> cookies()` with `List<Cookies> cookies(String name)`
